title: Check RMS screen for system faults as the first step during an OptiSweep support call
summary: During an OptiSweep support call, check the RMS / fleet status UI first to determine whether any system faults are present. This quickly establishes whether the issue is likely fleet-wide/system-level before deeper diagnostics.
when_to_use: Use at the start of a support call to answer: “Are there any system faults?” and to decide whether to proceed with deeper diagnostics based on whether system faults are visible on the RMS screen.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as the only step when the RMS screen is blank/unreachable; the segment indicates escalation is needed, but does not provide alternate access steps.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Open the RMS / fleet status UI and check for system-fault indications as the first evidence-gathering step on the call.
operator: If available, share what they see on the RMS screen (the segment notes that some callers may not be able to share screen and that an operator may need to guide/confirm what is shown).
access_or_tools_needed: RMS dashboard URL (provided to support users per segment)

access_required: Access to the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) via the provided RMS dashboard URL

visual_references.description: RMS page showing where system faults are displayed (system faults on the left; active AGV faults on the right).
RMS page behavior note: firewall not open can result in the RMS page showing blank.

steps.title: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (RMS screen) using the provided dashboard URL
steps.purpose: Establish the first evidence point on the call by checking whether system faults are present.
steps.instruction: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (RMS screen) using the provided RMS dashboard URL.
steps.expected_result: The RMS screen loads and is ready to view system-fault indications.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS screen is accessible and shows the system-fault area/list/status indicator.
steps.failure_condition: RMS screen cannot be accessed or does not load (e.g., shows blank).

actions.label: Open RMS dashboard
actions.exact_action: Go to that RMS screen (using the URL to the dashboard).

stop_or_escalate_if: RMS screen cannot be accessed or does not load (blank/unreachable).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “first thing first, go to that RMS screen, see if any system faults. This should always be your your first step on a phone call.”
“This page should show RMS, but the firewall is not open, so it just kind of shows blank.”

steps.title: Check the RMS screen for system-fault indications
steps.purpose: Determine whether the issue is likely fleet-wide/system-level by observing system faults on the RMS screen.
steps.instruction: On the RMS screen, look for the system-faults area/list/status indicator (system faults shown on the left).
steps.expected_result: You can observe whether system faults are present (system-fault indications visible) or absent (no system-fault indication shown).
steps.healthy_condition: No system-fault indication is shown in the system-faults area/list/status on the RMS screen.
steps.failure_condition: System-fault indications are present/visible on the RMS screen.

actions.label: Look for system faults
actions.exact_action: See if any system faults (system faults on the left).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “This page will show the Geek+ RMS web page … system faults on the left and any … active AGV faults on the right.”
“first thing first, go to that RMS screen, see if any system faults.”

steps.title: If system faults are present, record what is shown on the RMS screen
steps.purpose: Capture immediate evidence (fault indicators and any visible fault identifiers/status text) to guide next diagnostics.
steps.instruction: Record the system-fault indicators shown on the RMS screen, including any visible fault identifiers/status text.
steps.expected_result: A clear note exists describing the visible system-fault indicators and any fault identifiers/status text shown on the RMS screen.
steps.healthy_condition: N/A (this step applies only when system faults are present).
steps.failure_condition: System faults are present but no details are captured (no fault identifiers/status text recorded).

actions.label: Record system-fault details
actions.exact_action: Record what is shown (fault/system-fault indicators and any visible fault identifiers/status text).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “first thing first, go to that RMS screen, see if any system faults.”
System faults are displayed on the left of the RMS page.

steps.title: If no system faults are present, record absence and proceed with further evidence gathering
steps.purpose: Confirm that the RMS screen does not show system faults, so the call can focus on non-fleet-wide causes.
steps.instruction: Record that the RMS screen shows no system-fault indication, then proceed with further evidence gathering (the segment does not specify which next surfaces/steps to use).
steps.expected_result: A note exists stating that no system-fault indication is visible on the RMS screen.
steps.healthy_condition: No system-fault indication is shown on the RMS screen.
steps.failure_condition: System faults are present but you record that none are present (missed observation).

actions.label: Record no system faults
actions.exact_action: Record that the RMS screen shows no system-fault indication.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “first thing first, go to that RMS screen, see if any system faults.”

success_criteria: RMS / fleet status UI is opened successfully (or escalation is triggered if it cannot be accessed).
System-fault presence/absence is observed on the RMS screen and recorded (including visible fault identifiers/status text when present).
healthy_conditions: RMS screen shows system-faults area/list/status indicator with no system-fault indication when the system is healthy (for this check).
failure_conditions: RMS screen cannot be accessed or does not load (e.g., blank).
System-fault indications are visible on the RMS screen.
escalation_guidance: If the RMS screen cannot be accessed or does not load, escalate using the support process. (This segment does not provide alternate access steps.)
